newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's Aqaba port to expand industrial jetty.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's Aqaba port to expand industrial jetty.

text.p: Jordan has awarded a local and U.K. engineering partnership a design contract to expand an industrial berth in its Red Sea port of Aqaba to cater for higher fertiliser exports by the year 2000, industry sources said.

Jordan's Aqaba Port Authority signed the 326,000 dinar ($460,451) contract to design the expanded industrial jetty with U.K. based Rendal Palmer and Tritton and its local partner Amman-based engineering firm Consolidated Consultants.
The contract, to be completed in 230 days, also includes preparing tender documents for construction of the berth.
The expansion of the existing industrial berth is to cope with a forecast surge in fertiliser exports as new projects come on stream by end of the decade.
The project will allow the port to raise its handling capacity of industrial exports and imports to around eight million tonnes annually from a current three million tonnes, port officials said.

Another 130,000 dinar contract was awarded to the same partnership to advise on maintenance and repair of the existing nine berths in the main port. Maintenance tenders are expected to be spread over three years with 500,000 dinars allocated for 1997 alone, port officials said.
The port of Aqaba expanded rapidly in the 1980s to cater for its role as Iraq's main sea conduit during its war with Iran.
It has been positioning itself for months to handle an expected increase in Iraqi imports expected under an oil-for-food deal implemented earlier this month.
Business at Aqaba dropped sharply since the UN imposed sanctions on Iraq after its August 1990 invasion.
